definition: The randomized weighted majority algorithm is an algorithm in machine learning theory for aggregating expert predictions to a series of decision problems.
details: It is a simple and effective method based on weighted voting which improves on the mistake bound of the deterministic weighted majority algorithm. In fact, in the limit, its prediction rate can be arbitrarily close to that of the best-predicting expert.

explainer.lead: An algorithm in machine learning theory for aggregating expert predictions across a series of decision problems using weighted voting. It matters because it improves on the deterministic weighted majority algorithm's mistake bound and can approach the best expert's prediction rate.

tiers.eli5: You follow several advisers and shift your trust toward whichever has been right most often, so over time you do nearly as well as the best adviser.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it as a theoretically grounded way to combine expert or model predictions online; a pitfall is expecting it to beat the best expert outright rather than approach it in the limit.
tiers.paperLevel: A weighted-voting aggregation of expert predictions over a sequence of decision problems; it improves the mistake bound of the deterministic weighted majority algorithm, and in the limit its prediction rate can be arbitrarily close to that of the best-predicting expert.

explainer.example: Track weights for several forecasters on daily predictions, lowering the weight of any that err, so total mistakes stay near the best forecaster's.
